_purpose: Resolution for the two infant-formula cells no government regulates directly (mercury; hexavalent chromium). SUPERSEDES the earlier LOQ-non-detect-ceiling approach. HMTc sets a firm limit for every analyte and does NOT do 'monitored, not limited' — but the limit is a GOVERNMENT VALUE (read across from the nearest regulated product), not an HMTc-invented analytical floor. This keeps one basis class across the whole standard and preserves the sovereign-law defensibility shield for every cell.
_audit_trail: Evolved LOQ-non-detect-ceiling -> government-read-across. Audited against the 5 Governing Principles + a Daubert stress-test + FDA FY2009-2024 occurrence data (195 baby-food Hg samples: 76% non-detect, max 3.5 ppb, no product in the 5-20 band). Findings: (1) the ratchet/consumer-protection edge of a tighter ALARA floor (5) over the government read-across (20) is illusory in practice — no product sits between them and both are far below any health concern for the milk/soy matrix; (2) an ALARA floor introduces a SECOND basis class that breaks method consistency and opens the exact 'why is this number derived differently' Daubert seam Method v2.0 exists to close; (3) government read-across keeps every number a sovereign value. ALARA is NOT extended to initial limit-setting; it stays in its governing-doc line-185 role as the POST-PUBLICATION ratchet, available to tighten mercury later if surveillance ever shows category creep.

tHg.anchor: China GB 2762-2025 Table 3 total-mercury 20 ug/kg for CANNED COMPLEMENTARY FOODS for infants and young children (a different product form), applied to infant formula by read-across.
tHg.confirmation: No government sets a mercury ML for infant formula in any checked jurisdiction. Confirmed against the authoritative Codex CXS 193 current-2025 (Hg MLs only for mineral water, salt, six fish species), EU 2023/915 Annex I 3.3 (fish/salt/cereals only), and data/evidence/standards-no-ml-confirmed.csv. The nearest government value is China's 20.
tHg.read_across_label: read-across (nearest analogous product), not a formula-specific ML — must be labelled as such on the page.
tHg.feasibility_receipt: FDA FY2009-2024, 195 baby-food Hg samples: 76% non-detect (ICP-MS), detected range 0.2-3.5 ppb; formula (milk/soy) runs cleaner than the rice cereals that produced every detection. 100% of observed product clears 20 with enormous margin.
tHg.post_publication: ALARA ratchet (Governing Principles line 185) tightens this if category surveillance ever shows mercury above the clean-platform floor.

Cr-total.anchor: China GB 2762-2025 Table 7 total-chromium 2.0 mg/kg (2000 ug/kg) for milk powder and modified milk powder (dairy), applied to infant formula by read-across. GB 2762-2025 (effective 2026-09-02) keeps this value unchanged from GB 2762-2022 (diffed 2026-08-04).
Cr-total.read_across_label: read-across from the dairy milk-powder category; label as such.

Cr-VI.control: No government sets a Cr-VI limit for any food (only total Cr). Cr-VI is registered not-material for infant formula (Saraiva 2021: does not persist in the matrix; near-total reduction to Cr-III). It is CONTROLLED through the total-chromium limit (2000, above) with MANDATORY Cr-VI speciation on any total-Cr result above 100 ug/kg; any quantifiable Cr-VI fails certification.
Cr-VI.not_monitored_only: This is a limit, not 'monitored, not limited': the material analyte (total Cr) carries a firm government number, and confirmed Cr-VI at any quantifiable level is a hard fail.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Saraiva 2021 SS-ID-HPLC-ICP-MS, LOQ ~0.05 ug/kg (the corpus's citable named speciation method).
